## Before class

Read Speegle and Clair, [*Probability, Statistics, and Data*, §§2.1, 2.2, and
2.4](https://probstatsdata.com/probchapter.html). Bring your laptop with RStudio
ready to use. **A1 is due at the beginning of class.**

Conditional probability and Bayes' rule (§2.3) are for September 16, alongside
the assigned Blitzstein and Hwang Chapter 2 reading.

## By the end of the seminar

You should be able to define a sample space and event, distinguish equally
likely from unequally likely outcomes, use complement and union rules, and
calculate finite probabilities by counting when the assumptions permit it.

You should also be able to simulate a complete trial with `sample()`, repeat
trials with `replicate()`, and estimate an event probability using a logical
comparison and `mean()`. We will compare exact and simulated answers using dice,
random treatment assignment, hypothetical polling, and committee selection.
